personalityDossier.fullText:
THE THREE-CAT MASTER PERSONALITY DOSSIER
ONYX BLEPMAN • CALLIE ROUND • HARVEY SQUARE
Unified family personality bible | November 1, 2026

======================================================================
PURPOSE AND SOURCE STANDARD
======================================================================

This document merges the cat-specific personality material in:
  • ONYX_MASTER_MERGED_PERSONALITY(8)(1).txt
  • Callie_Harvey_Master_Personality_Adventures_Dossier(10).txt

It concerns the THREE CATS AS INDIVIDUALS: their observed traits, reported
habits, appearances, preferences, family relationships, communication,
memorable anecdotes, nicknames, and shared household culture. It is not a
technical specification, a care schedule, or a veterinary assessment.

The descriptions distinguish three kinds of material:
  REPORTED: behavior or an incident attributed to the family, including the
  family songs and descriptions summarized in the supplied dossiers.
  FAMILY LORE: affectionate anthropomorphism, office titles, nicknames, and
  comic interpretations of the cats' conduct.
  INTERPRETATION: a cautious reading of how the reported patterns fit together.

A family nickname does not literally make a cat a government official, a
psychiatrist, or an employee. Likewise, apparent conversational awareness is
not a claim that a cat understands human language as a person would. The
humor is preserved because it records what makes each cat recognizable.

No exact ages, unconfirmed ancestry, coat-patch maps, diagnoses, or histories
are assigned to Callie or Harvey. The anecdotes about human food are records
of curiosity and household stories, not feeding recommendations. Onyx's
service history is described as family-reported and is not a substitute for
formal medical or training records.

======================================================================
PART I — LORD ONYX BLEPMAN
EMPEROR OF THE VOIDATTUDE
======================================================================

01. IDENTITY AT A GLANCE

Onyx is a large, black, senior cat, described as part Maine Coon, with
notable green-gold eyes, long whiskers, a serious face, and a striking
preference for his bowtie. The family reports his weight at approximately
27 pounds. Those physical qualities are distinctive, but his personality
cannot be reduced to the appearance of an imposing black cat.

His central character is an extraordinary combination of committed
attachment, practical and social attentiveness, routine, comfort-seeking,
expressive complaint, food opportunism, stubborn autonomy, and context-
sensitive seriousness. He can be the sleepiest cat in the room and still
behave as if the entire room falls under his supervision.

The family's most accurate shorthand is "protective attachment wrapped in
theatrical entitlement." He takes up space, insists on being understood,
expects familiar conditions to remain familiar, and makes a production of
minor inconveniences. Yet this is an intensely affectionate cat. The
complaining takes place inside the relationship rather than signaling a
wish to leave it.

He is the Emperor who wants to be the baby; the baby who expects to be
treated like the Emperor. His affection is physical. His independence is
real. His judgments can be severe-looking, while his loyalty stays put.

02. THE EMPEROR'S GOVERNING TEMPERAMENT

Onyx appears to regard family life as a shared operation in which he has
standing. He cares where Papa lies, whether the blanket is correct, when
food is served, where his bowtie has gone, who is speaking to him, and
whether somebody has disrupted a chosen resting position. A complaint is
not simply a complaint. In family mythology, it is an imperial grievance.

He has strong expectations of reliability. He anticipates food, comfort,
attention, familiar touch, known voices, and habitual procedures. He is
comfortable enough in the household to be inconvenient: he can sprawl,
refuse to relocate, require a blanket adjustment, or deliver a long
"sermon" without acting as if affection will disappear afterward.

That mix is why he is so funny. The household can interpret a missing
blanket as a constitutional crisis because he has the certainty of a
creature who knows he belongs. His grumpiness coexists with trust.

Onyx is not merely an irritable elder. He is a securely attached,
conspicuously opinionated participant in family decisions. His sense of
entitlement is one of the ways his confidence becomes visible.

03. HOW ONYX COMMUNICATES

Onyx has a rich, recognizable collection of sounds and body signals.
Reported vocal behavior includes meows, yowls, grumbles, groans, huffs,
and sustained "grumble-grumble sermons." He can make a point and then
make the same point more firmly when it has not been acknowledged.

His face also speaks. Fixed stares, narrowing eyes, side-eye, changes in
ear and pupil position, and offended postures produce the family image of
a stern elderly gentleman inspecting the decisions of others.

Physical communication is especially important: he can lean, climb,
paw, knead, stroke a person to request petting, occupy a pathway, or
position himself directly on the person whose attention he wants. His
preferred locations are not random. He repeatedly chooses Papa's legs,
chests, pillows, furniture, higher vantage points, and other places where
his body means something to the people around him.

Persistence links the signals together. A stare becomes a sound. A sound
can become a repeated sound. A request can become a paw or scratching.
He seems willing to revise his tactics until the message gets through.

The family affectionately says Onyx "speaks fluent human." This means
his reactions often seem well timed and contextually appropriate, not
that anyone has established humanlike language comprehension. Years of
close observation have made Onyx and his people fluent in one another's
habits and expectations.

04. SOCIAL INTELLIGENCE AND PRACTICAL LEARNING

The source dossiers emphasize Onyx's social intelligence more than
abstract problem-solving. He appears attentive to which person is speaking,
which action results in food, who tolerates a kind of touch, which signal
is likely to be effective, and which deviations from routine are worth
challenging.

He has reportedly learned sit, stay, come, up, down, pose, sit pretty,
and high-five. He has traveled on a leash and in a stroller and worked
alongside William as a service animal. These reports convey trainability,
structured cooperation, and an interest in being involved.

The most memorable impression, however, comes from timing. He protests
when something changes, responds differently to different family members,
and can shift from ordinary domestic negotiation to concentrated attention.
His apparent intelligence is therefore inseparable from relationship.

He is not a generic "clever cat" who performs every trick for everyone.
His skills and reactions seem embedded in particular people, places,
routines, and consequences.

05. PAPA / WILLIAM: BEST FRIEND AND HOME BASE

William describes Onyx as his best friend. Their relationship reaches
across more than a decade of adult life, changing states and homes,
housing instability, travel, disability, medical experiences, and major
changes in the family. Onyx's familiar bodily closeness carries all of
that shared history.

Onyx sleeps across William, on his chest, and particularly on the backs
of his legs. He may knead, purr, stretch, lean, sprawl, and treat Papa's
body as reliable furniture. That reliance is comical and deeply trusting
at the same time.

The relationship also has a peer-like quality. William is the trusted
human, longstanding companion, service partner, food provider, bowtie
restorer, preferred resting place, and person to supervise. Onyx may
accept care without accepting every manner of being addressed. In the
family account, he generally objects when Papa uses baby talk.

This is not a simple parent-and-dependent relationship. William has cared
for Onyx through hard conditions. Onyx has reportedly watched, responded
to, alerted, and protected William. Their history gives ordinary cuddling
the meaning of an old partnership.

06. MOMMA / JASPER: THE AFFECTIONATE EXCEPTION

Jasper has a distinct relationship with Onyx, not an interchangeable
version of William's bond. Jasper is permitted to baby-talk him, cup his
face, scoop and cuddle him, give him outrageous nicknames, play around
with his bowtie, and sometimes place objects on his head during affectionate
fooling around. Onyx may grumble through such indignities while remaining
comfortable and engaged.

The supplied history recalls Jasper in Onyx's chosen spot in 2023, with
Onyx behind them looking like a suspicious landlord. Later family photos
and descriptions portray affectionate cradling, hugging, carrying, and
cuddling. Jasper became a trusted parent with a uniquely permissive set of
social rules.

Momma can call him Onion, Bunion, Onion Fart, or Mr. Poop Poop, and this
is part of their special relationship. Onyx's protests can be part of the
ritual instead of a withdrawal of affection. Jasper can also intervene
when Onyx's decision to remain on William's legs has become impractical.

His different conduct with William and Jasper is fundamental. Onyx is
selective, not indiscriminately tolerant. Being intensely loved does not
erase his boundaries; instead, his trusted people have different kinds
of permission.

07. THE WORKING-CAT SWITCH

Onyx is described as a real service cat with reported alert and response
work involving William's medical and trauma-related needs. At ordinary
times, Onyx may be deeply asleep, demanding food, kneading, or indulging
in old-man complaints. When a situation matters, he has reportedly
become sharply attentive, persistent, and physically direct.

That change is the "working-cat switch." He can stop being an offended
muffin and concentrate. The qualities that make him difficult to ignore
when hungry—observation, persistence, communication, and willingness to
use his body—also appear in the family's account of his service work.

The most consequential story describes a train/subway incident in 2018.
According to William's account, corroborated in the family's telling by
witnesses, Onyx left an open stroller he ordinarily stayed in, launched
himself against William's chest during a dangerous moment near an incoming
train, altered his movement, and returned. This remains a family-reported
incident. Its personality significance is Onyx's apparent willingness to
break a familiar rule when he perceived something urgent.

The source deliberately refuses to portray Onyx as a solemn hero every
minute. The same cat who could act protectively is also an old man
complaining about dinner and behaving as if a displaced blanket is an
emergency. Those are not different cats. They are different sides of a
recognizable individual.

08. HISTORY, RESILIENCE, AND RETURN

During periods of homelessness and unstable housing, Onyx reportedly
explored outdoors, traveled with William, and hunted birds. He could
leave the immediate area and return. The meaningful pattern for the
family is not only his independence but his return to William.

The source draws a distinction between physical surroundings and emotional
home. When addresses, rooms, and circumstances changed, William remained
a familiar person and point of return. Onyx later became highly particular
about blankets, soft beds, fans, pillows, routines, and formalwear. His
comfort standards are funnier because they follow a history that was not
always comfortable.

He has also adapted to different locations, public travel, leash walking,
and stroller use. The family does not interpret this as proof that he
loves all novelty. His apparent adaptability may depend on familiar
people and routines accompanying him through unfamiliar places.

09. PRESSURE, PROXIMITY, AND PHYSICAL AFFECTION

Onyx has a strongly physical way of showing attachment. He places weight
on his people, seeks sustained contact, purrs, kneads according to the
source accounts, moves closer, and returns to favorite resting positions.
His considerable size can make him feel like a living weighted blanket.

One especially specific routine involves the backs of William's legs.
In cooler weather, William may arrange himself so Onyx can lie there;
Onyx expects an appropriate blanket beneath him. If the configuration
is unacceptable, he may grumble, reposition, and object again. Affection
becomes a negotiation over furniture standards.

The family jokes that Papa is not merely a human but an important piece
of infrastructure. The tenderness beneath the joke is obvious: Onyx
trusts William's body as a safe, familiar place to sleep.

He also has a "Rotisserie Cat" tendency to reposition himself for
attention, warmth, or more favorable access to petting. Even his lounging
can feel active and purposeful.

10. COMFORT ENGINEERING: BLANKETS, FANS, AND PILLOWS

Onyx prefers soft surfaces, familiar textures, appropriate blankets,
specific sleeping positions, and dependable personal spaces. A favorite
pillow, ottoman, elevated bookshelf perch, chair, stroller, bed, or
piece of occupied human furniture can become part of his routine.

The source emphasizes that he reportedly enjoys strong airflow from
fans even while seeking contact and warmth. His ideal may involve being
snuggled and weighted against a familiar person without becoming too
warm. He is not inconsistent so much as exacting about a combination of
comfort variables.

His requirements are sensory and social: softness, temperature, airflow,
pressure, scent, elevation, familiarity, security, and proximity. Once
he likes a particular arrangement, he can treat it as established policy.

"Blanket engineering has failed" is the family interpretation of a cat
who knows the difference between the position he expected and the one
he was actually offered.

11. THE BOWTIE GENTLEMAN

The bowtie is one of Onyx's clearest individual markers. The supplied
family descriptions distinguish it from an ordinary collar: he reportedly
likes the bowtie and expects it to be put back after it is removed for
scratchies. He may lower or bow his head to assist with reapplication.

William is described as the preferred person to restore it, while Jasper
has unusual permission to remove it temporarily or joke with it. In
family lore, an undressed Onyx is "naked" and an appropriately bowtied
Onyx has regained his ceremonial dignity.

The familiar green plaid bowtie, black coat, green-gold eyes, large
whiskers, and serious gaze form a strongly recognizable portrait. The
bowtie expresses routine, identity, cooperative trust, and a standard of
personal presentation that seems deeply Onyx.

12. BLEPS, GRUMBLES, AND DIGNITY MALFUNCTIONS

The name "Blepman" celebrates the tongue that occasionally protrudes
from the face of an otherwise imposing cat. Onyx may look stern or
ancient, like a scholar silently reviewing the household, only for his
blep to undo the entire majestic presentation.

This contradiction is part of his appeal. He is dignified and goofy,
serious and ridiculous, confident and soft, ancient-looking and
babyish. A perfectly imperial expression can collapse into pure cat
nonsense in a moment.

His grumbles work similarly. They may accompany petting, cuddling,
repositioning, dressing, and even situations where he plainly remains
attached to the person he is "complaining" about. The family hears
those grumbles as commentary, not necessarily rejection.

13. THE VICTORIAN CHILD AND FOOD POLITICS

Food is a major feature of Onyx's social life. He watches distribution,
notices who is eating, and treats meals as household events in which he
ought to have a say. Wet food becomes tribute; human food becomes an
opportunity for investigation; the bowl is a site of negotiation.

The supplied histories describe particular interest in beef Gravy Lovers
Fancy Feast, tuna juice, catnip treats, and a wide assortment of human
foods or food smells. Those anecdotes include milk, yogurt, pudding,
meat, cheese flavors, donuts, and other things that should not be treated
as dietary advice. The personality point is opportunism and curiosity,
not a recommended menu.

He reportedly uses different tactics with different people. Momma is a
prominent begging target. With Papa, protest may escalate into repeated
signals and paw-based persuasion. The family imagines him calculating
food portions and arguing about taxation.

"Victorian Child" describes the sound of his food-related melodrama.
Dinner can be only slightly late, yet Onyx vocalizes as though a Dickensian
workhouse has denied him sustenance since the nineteenth century. The
drama is affectionate comedy because the family knows he is cared for.

Food is also an invitation to belong. When people eat, Onyx wants to be
part of the occasion. His apparent grievance is not only "I am hungry"
but "Why was I excluded from this decision?"

14. SENIORITY: OLD MAN MUFFIN

Onyx's senior age has intensified the personality he already had. He is
still observant, persistent, affectionate, demanding, food-aware, and
routine-loving. Now those preferences carry the authority of long habit.
He knows his places, his sounds, his people, his ceremonies, and his
standards.

"Old Man Muffin" captures an elder who can be both profoundly sleepy
and thoroughly babied. He is senior enough to seem to have tenure in
every domestic dispute, and soft enough to be treated as a precious
infant by his family.

He does not need constant activity to be present. His resting presence,
weight, small movements, and occasional offended noises are themselves
recognizable Onyx behaviors.

15. INDEPENDENCE, SELECTIVITY, AND BOUNDARIES

Onyx's affection is intense but not indiscriminate. He can explore,
choose a high perch, refuse to move, dislike certain handling or tones,
and express dissent through sound, posture, ear position, withdrawal,
or stubborn stillness. He is neither merely aloof nor helplessly clingy.

His trust allows closeness. He permits different forms of handling from
William and Jasper, cooperates with familiar rituals, and sleeps deeply
on people he knows. His willingness to stay close does not mean he has
lost the ability to make preferences known.

The clearest synthesis is: Onyx loves intensely without surrendering his
sense of self. He can protest and remain. He can explore and return.
He can object to a procedure and still seek the person carrying it out.

16. PLAY, HUNTING, AND PRACTICAL INTERESTS

The family material describes Onyx as less interested in some ordinary
cat toys and laser pointers than in people, food, environments,
meaningful interaction, and historically real hunting. This is a
preference reported about this individual, not a claim that ordinary
cat play is beneath cats generally.

His family jokingly describes him as a "practical cat" who has reviewed
a laser-pointer pursuit without a real outcome and found the business model lacking. What
is actually visible is that Onyx seems most responsive to activities
connected with his relationships, surroundings, or concrete interests.

His hunting history is part of his biography, but it does not erase the
present-day senior who would rather find the right blanket and nap.

17. SONGS AND PERSON-SPECIFIC RITUALS

William sings "Baby Mine" to Onyx. Jasper has an affectionate,
personalized musical ritual built around Onyx as an infant void with
absurd nicknames. These rituals have different tones: William's is
linked with longtime tenderness; Jasper's with playful babying,
face-cupping, and permission to be ridiculous.

The sources do not establish that Onyx understands song lyrics. They
record familiar voice, melody, rhythm, touch, and repeated attention as
features of how he is loved. Family songs are part of the environment
through which he recognizes people and is recognized by them.

18. AN ENTIRE ECOLOGY OF NICKNAMES

The merged Onyx source records an unusually extensive list, including:

  Lord Onyx Blepman, Emperor of the Voidattude
  Sir Onyx Newton from the Land of Derpitude
  Void Boy Genius
  Sweet Baby Onion Fart
  Baby Bobungus
  Baby Fungus Bungus
  Onion Lad / Onion / Bunion / Onion Fart
  Old Man Muffin / The Muffin Man / Huffin Muffin / Man Muffin
  Grumbly Lad
  Onyx Poop Poop / Mr. Poop Poop
  Beautiful Little Parasite
  Rotisserie Cat
  Chungus
  Bookshelf Gargoyle
  Tiny Void Emperor
  Bowtie-Crowned King
  Tiny Bowtie Professor
  Victorian Child

The family uses these names as a kind of affectionate shorthand.
"Grumbly Lad" is sound. "Rotisserie Cat" is movement. "Bookshelf
Gargoyle" is the high-perch stare. "Victorian Child" is the food
sermon. "Blepman" is the tongue that ruins solemnity. "Beautiful
Little Parasite" is the cat who monopolizes resources while giving
back companionship and laughter.

"Tiny Bowtie Professor" and "Emperor" are playful titles about his
expression and perceived authority, not claims of human occupations.

19. JUDGMENT WITHOUT WITHDRAWAL

Onyx can look as though he is evaluating every human mistake. The source
includes his seeming disapproval of William and Jasper flirting, his
stares over disputed sleeping spots, and his protests during affectionate
handling. Yet the relationship continues. He may judge the person and
then sleep on them.

This is a defining difference between actual conflict and family comedy.
In the family's reading, Onyx's stare says, "I have documented the
violation," not "I no longer belong to you."

His stern appearance and his strong attachment are simultaneous truths.
The Emperor judges; the best friend stays.

20. COMMITTED PRESENCE AND EMOTIONAL ANCHORING

Onyx's most consistent love language, in human metaphor, is sustained
presence. He stays nearby, comes back, lies on familiar bodies, watches
changes, touches, complains, alerts, travels, and returns to his people's
immediate world. Even asleep, he changes the family's sense of space.

His weight, purring, breathing, scent, warmth, and consistent routines
can be grounding to people who know him. The supplied analysis describes
him as a living orientation point through difficult experiences, not a
magical healer or an animal who must always perform a job.

He has shaped family language: songs, nicknames, grievance jokes, blanket
procedures, cherished photographs, and the shared stories that define
home. Onyx is not loved only because of his service history. He is
loved because he is Onyx in all the silly and ordinary hours as well.

21. THE FAMILY'S "FORMERLY HUMAN" MYTHOLOGY

William has described Onyx as so socially attentive and individual that
living with him has made ideas about consciousness or reincarnation feel
more imaginable. The supplied master dossier treats this as the family's
personal interpretation, not evidence that reincarnation has been proved.

The feeling arises from Onyx's strong routines, contextual reactions,
distinct relationships, dignity, social exceptions, apparent conversation,
and elderly-gentleman demeanor. The family experiences a substantial,
continuous individual behind his eyes.

His personality does not require a supernatural explanation to be
meaningful. The observation that matters is how recognizably and
consistently he has been himself across years of change.

22. ONYX IN ONE COMPLETE PORTRAIT

Onyx is a protective, opinionated, expressive senior with a formidable
sense of routine and a profound bond with his family. He loves weight,
closeness, comfort, familiar people, competent arrangements, and a
well-placed bowtie. He notices patterns, communicates persistently,
learns practical tasks, and can become focused when the situation
requires it. He also bleps, complains, solicits food with theatrical
urgency, and turns William's legs into an imperially regulated bed.

His signature paradox is that he can be loyal and demanding, independent
and attached, stern and goofy, sleepy and vigilant, dignified and
hilariously undignified—without ceasing to be the same cat.

======================================================================
PART II — CALLIE ROUND
THE TORTOISESHELL HR DIRECTOR AND SENTIENT MEATBALL
======================================================================

23. IDENTITY AT A GLANCE

Callie is the family's tortoiseshell cat: fluffy, expressive, and notably
committed to comfortable positions of her own choosing. The family calls
her Callie Round, a "sentient meatball," and a "judgmental bowling ball."
These descriptions emphasize her dense, cozy presence and how difficult
she can be to persuade to move once she has settled.

Her signature temperament combines stubborn comfort, a disapproving
looking stare, seat-claiming determination, remarkable fur production,
powerful food-related vocalization, and sudden bursts of genuine play.

Callie is not merely an inert or grumpy cat. She participates in chases
with Harvey and has a playful side that contrasts sharply with her
usual air of immovable authority. Her affection is quieter than Harvey's
high-speed exuberance and different from Onyx's imperial demands.

24. THE HR DIRECTOR

"HR" is Callie's family office title. It works because of the serious,
patient, apparently unimpressed way she can regard the world, especially
Onyx's endless imagined complaints. A single long stare can suggest a
final decision. Onyx may spend minutes delivering a grievance; Callie
looks as if the matter was resolved before he began.

The joke is that Callie seems capable of denying the Emperor's appeal
while maintaining a few strong property claims of her own. She does not
need to be louder than Onyx. Her authority comes from remaining where
she has chosen to sit.

This is affectionate family lore, not evidence that Callie is unkind.
Her apparent judgment should never be confused with a permanently angry
temperament. She can be warm, comfortable, playful, and close to the
others while looking very serious.

25. OWNERSHIP OF CHAIRS AND SELECTED SPOTS

The family's songs describe Callie taking Momma's office chair, Papa's
wheelchair, and whichever other seat a person intended to use. Once
she chooses a spot, it ceases to be available for routine human plans.
The joke rests in her magnificent refusal to budge.

She can compress herself into a tight loaf, tuck her paws, lower her body,
and make the possibility of moving her seem like a complicated negotiation.
"Bowling-ball protest" is the family's metaphor for this substantial,
relaxed deadweight, not a claim that she literally becomes a ball or
that her stubbornness is fear.

The seat-stealing anecdotes show a recognizable preference for owning
comfort through stillness. She does not need to defend a chair with
constant activity. Possession is accomplished simply by being there.

26. THE FLOOF GOOF POOF POOF

Callie's abundant coat is central to the family's experience of her.
She is described as dense, soft, and exceptionally shed-happy. Brushing
can produce so much loose fur that the family jokes about constructing
an entirely new small creature from it.

Her floof and her round resting shapes create the affectionate
"meatball" association. She remains a cat, with distinct tortoiseshell
markings and ordinary feline anatomy; the comic roundness chiefly comes
from how she settles, curls, tucks, and becomes thoroughly comfortable.

The visual humor of Callie is very different from Harvey's sock-footed
speed and Onyx's broad black dignity. Callie looks like she has chosen
the optimal resting shape and intends to maintain it until further notice.

27. FOOD VOICE: TURKEY, HAM, AND THE SHEBA BOWL

The family songs describe Callie as a turkey and ham enthusiast with a
strong interest in her Sheba bowl. They compare the strength of her
food vocals to "Kelly Clarkson lungs." This is a humorous description
of the force and clarity of her demands.

Her food communication differs from Onyx's. Onyx sounds, in family lore,
like an offended Victorian monarch pleading his case. Callie is more
of a direct, confident announcer who expects the catering department to
hear her immediately.

She may appear almost inseparable from her chair until a familiar food
cue makes movement worthwhile. This sudden change from resting stone to
purposeful cat is one of her comic signatures.

The turkey and ham references are preserved as household anecdotes,
not as instructions to serve human processed meats to a cat.

28. OWL EYES AND THE POWER OF THE STARE

One family song describes Callie's eyes as seeming to look directly
through a person's soul. She has an alert, penetrating, evaluative
presence that makes the HR metaphor especially apt.

A long look, small head movement, or unhurried blink can communicate a
great deal. Her facial expressiveness often derives from restraint. She
does not need Onyx's prolonged lecture or Harvey's elaborate activity
to tell the family that something has been noticed.

Callie's gaze should not be equated with aggression. An affectionate,
settled cat can have an absolutely formidable resting expression.

29. COMFORT, WARMTH, AND "TOASTING HER BEANS"

Callie is especially associated with finding and defending pleasant
places to rest. William has anticipated that she will enjoy lying in
front of an electric fireplace in the family's prospective home and
"toasting her beans." This is an expectation, not evidence that a
future fireplace habit has already occurred.

The image is consistent with the rest of her characterization: a warm,
comfortable spot becomes an important appointment, paws may be stretched
out, and getting up is optional so far as Callie is concerned.

Her comfort is not simply laziness. It is an active preference, a way
of settling securely into a favorite place and making it hers.

30. SURPRISING ZOOMIES AND CHASES

Callie's stationary tendencies are only half her personality. The
family has reported household chase scenes between Callie and Harvey,
sometimes loud enough to disturb resting Onyx. Callie can chase, be
chased, turn, pounce, and suddenly move with surprising speed.

That contrast matters. A Callie who was just a perfectly immovable loaf
may become fully absorbed in play, then return to the quiet composure
she seems to prefer much of the time.

She is not a passive object beside a more athletic sister. She is a
participant in their relationship, sometimes responding to Harvey's
provocations and sometimes taking part in the rush herself.

31. AFFECTION AND SOFTNESS UNDER THE JUDGMENT

The family's comic descriptions are sharp, but their affection for
Callie is unambiguous. William and Jasper love her fluff, stolen seats,
